notes: Lead: IronReach (federal-adjacent critical operator) — heavy focus on air-gapped on-prem deployment. Key asks: 1) signed, verifiable appliance images that can be imported into their isolated datacenter; 2) HSM-backed key management and FIPS/TAA-compatible crypto; 3) attestation (TPM) + secure boot + SBOM for all binaries; 4) offline model loading workflow (no egress) and deterministic model provenance; 5) integration hooks to Splunk and existing SIEM, but only via pull of logs into a staging network — no outbound telemetry from production nodes. Quoted from SecOps: "We cannot allow any model or runtime to phone home — chain of custody and supply chain verification is mandatory." Procurement constraints: agency requires Authority to Operate (ATO) package — need STIG/CIS baseline checklist and evidence. Risk concerns: export control on some quantized weights, legal wants clarity on license/redistribution for model artifacts. Technical constraints: prefer isolated rack with 2-4 GPU nodes (A100-class) for POC, GPU drivers must be FIPS-compatible build; no internet DNS resolution on management plane. Performance targets (POC): median chat latency < 350ms for 8 concurrent analysts on short-context prompts; embeddings for search indexed nightly, reranking tail latency < 200ms. Cost sensitivity: willing to pay premium for air-gapped readiness but needs clear TCO for dedicated on-prem hardware + software license. POC proposal discussed: 6-week engagement, Redwood to provide signed appliance images, installation runbook, basic eval scripts and evaluation harness (privacy-preserving), security questionnaire and STIG evidence. Legal asks: indemnity language for classified data handling, a clear path for model updates (signed patches only).
